notes: Basis for candidacy: T:p1-b6 explicitly says that discovered B-type halo HVSs move faster than the Galactic escape speed, and T:p1-b10 describes the previously identified late B-type halo HVS population. T:p14-b0 (Table A1, titled "The Observational Sample of HVSs") lists HVS1, HVS4, HVS9, HVS10, HVS13, HVS15, HVS16, HVS18, HVS19, HVS20, HVS21, HVS22, HVS24, HVS5, HVS6, B129, B329, B458, HVS7, HVS8, HVS12, HVS17, B481, B576, and B1085; the M/G superscripts are sample-membership flags, not separate identifiers. At T:p13-b3, HVS1 is discarded only from the MMT+Gaia sample, HVS7/HVS8/HVS12/HVS17 are removed from the final MMT sample because previous work suggested non-GC origins, HVS5/HVS6 are retained despite controversial origins, and B129/B329/B458 are added to MMT+Gaia. B481/B576/B1085 lack M/G flags and are not described as members of either fitting sample. HVS3 at T:p7-b1 is only a previously discovered halo-HVS/HVB-or-blue-straggler candidate used for comparison; no individual velocity or component identifiers are given. S5-HVS1 at T:p10-b4 is a previously discovered HVS distinct from the table object HVS1; the paper models its likely CWD origin.

HVS1: Table A1 (T:p14-b0) provides Galactocentric distance (R^M, R^G) and velocity (v^M, v^G) for HVS1; these velocities are those of halo HVSs quoted in the Galactic rest frame (T:p1-b10). No heliocentric distance, parallax, equatorial coordinates, proper motion, or radial velocity is reported for HVS1. HVS1 is excluded from the MMT+Gaia sample per Appendix C ("HVS1 is discarded as it becomes a clear outlier in terms of the Galactocentric distance"), though its values are still listed.

HVS4: Table A1 reports HVS4 with both original (MMT) and Gaia-corrected (MMT+Gaia) velocity and Galactocentric distance; both are retained without choosing a preferred value (T:p14-b0). The velocity columns are treated as Galactic-rest-frame velocities, consistent with the paper's description of halo HVS velocities.

HVS9: HVS9 has the superscript M,G, so it is included in both the MMT and MMT+Gaia samples.
